title: U.S. House · California's 41st District
area: Eastern Los Angeles County, including cities such as Whittier, La Habra Heights, Diamond Bar and Walnut. The district was redrawn by Proposition 50 (approved November 2025) and no longer overlaps the Riverside County territory the old 41st District held.

context.text: California's 41st District was redrawn after voters approved Proposition 50 in November 2025, part of a mid-decade, multi-state redistricting round. Analyst Nathaniel Rakich of Inside Elections described the new 41st, previously represented by Republican Ken Calvert, as a D+16 seat in eastern Los Angeles County that would be a near-automatic Democratic pickup. Rep. Linda Sánchez, who currently represents the old 38th District, is running here instead; incumbent Ken Calvert is not on the ballot for this seat.

candidates.name: Linda Sánchez
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Linda Sánchez is a Democrat and former labor lawyer who has served in the U.S. House since 2002, representing the 38th District since 2013, and is running in the redrawn 41st District. She sits on the Ways and Means Committee, where she is the ranking member of the Trade Subcommittee. According to her campaign, she is running on lowering costs.

background.text: Born in Orange, California, in 1969, the sixth of seven children of immigrant parents from Mexico; her father was an industrial machinist and mechanic and her mother an elementary school teacher, according to her official biography.

Earned a bachelor's degree in Spanish literature from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1991 and a law degree from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1995; she worked as a bilingual aide and ESL instructor while in school.

Practiced appellate, civil rights and employment law, then worked as a compliance officer for IBEW Local 441 and the National Electrical Contractors Association; in 2000 she was elected executive director of the Orange County Central Labor Council, AFL-CIO.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2002 at age 34 from a new district created after the 2000 Census, becoming the first woman IBEW member elected to Congress. Her sister Loretta Sánchez served in the House from 1997 to 2017.
Represented the old 39th District from 2003, and won re-election in 2012 in the 38th District after redistricting; she most recently represented the 38th.

Serves on the Ways and Means Committee, having been the first Latina on both Ways and Means and the Judiciary Committee; since 2024 she has been ranking member of the Trade Subcommittee. She also served on the Select Committee on Benghazi from 2014 to 2016.

Her official biography credits her with introducing the Gender Equity in Health Premiums Act in 2009, which became part of the Affordable Care Act, and with 2016 bipartisan legislation on tax deductions for caregivers of relatives.
Her official biography says she is the mother of a son, Joaquín, born in 2009, and lists her as one of the few women to play in the Congressional Baseball Game.
Following California's 2025 redistricting (Proposition 50), she is running in the newly drawn 41st District in the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for Southern California families, including housing and grocery costs.
Making health care more affordable, including restoring Medicaid funding, protecting ACA subsidies and lowering prescription drug costs.

positions.summary: Says she is fighting to restore Medicaid funding, protect Affordable Care Act subsidies, lower prescription drug costs and ensure no one is denied coverage.

Cosponsored H.R. 4876, the Reproductive Freedom for Veterans Act, a bill to direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide abortion care, counseling, and related services and medication to certain individuals (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, a bill to regulate assault weapons (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025, a bill to provide for increases in the federal minimum wage (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 8085, the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act of 2026 (a tax on the net value of assets of a taxpayer) and H.R. 5427, the Billionaires Income Tax Act (119th Congress).
Said in a campaign statement that she will not vote to fund ICE until the agency is reformed, and called for body cameras for agents and background checks for new hires.
positions.quote: In Congress, I refuse to send another penny to fund ICE until we fully reform the organization and rebuild it from the ground up.

record.text: Passed legislation to ban hedge funds from buying up single-family homes, according to her campaign.
Passed a law barring health insurers from charging women more than men for the same coverage, according to her campaign.

candidates.name: Mitch Clemmons
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Mitch Clemmons is the Republican candidate for California's 41st District. He is a plumbing contractor and small-business owner who has operated his own plumbing company since 2002. He ran unsuccessfully for state Senate in 2022 and has not held elected office.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Santa Fe High School.
Studied aerospace engineering technology at California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, according to Ballotpedia.
Worked as a warehouse manager for Lantis Eyewear before starting a plumbing company that he has operated since 2002.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, describes himself as a family man, local plumbing contractor and small business owner who has helped employees earn plumbing licenses and start their own businesses.
Ran for California State Senate District 30 in 2022 as a Republican; he advanced from the primary but lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Bob Archuleta, 61% to 39%.

priorities.text: Election integrity, saying secure and transparent elections are the foundation for addressing law and order, protecting children and stopping government waste and fraud.
priorities.quote: Election integrity is the foundation of everything we care about. If our elections are not secure and transparent, voters cannot choose the right leaders or pass the right policies — period.

priorities.text: Restoring law and order, treating homelessness humanely while holding people accountable and cracking down on small crimes early.
Protecting children and parents' rights, with schools that teach skills and values rather than ideology.

positions.summary: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey (state Senate race), said he is a proponent of school choice.
positions.quote: I am a proponent of school choice, as parents should be able to choose to send their students to a school that will provide the best education possible.

candidates.researchNotes: Limited public record: 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (priorities only) and a 2022 survey from his state Senate run (school choice, dated 2022). No campaign website was located.
